newsitem.title: UK: Brazil alcohol output seen below plan - Czarnikow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil alcohol output seen below plan - Czarnikow.

text.p: Brazilian alcohol production in 1997/98 is expected to reach 15.2 billion litres and fall short of the government crop plan by some 1.5 billion litres, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.

"It is difficult to predict the split between sugar and alcohol but the crop plan requirement of 16.73 billion litres of alcohol for the country is likely to be more than will be needed by quite a margin," it said.
The plan's figure might have reflected government caution over supplies during the first year of deregulation for anhydrous alcohol.

The remaining cane would be sufficient to produce about 15.5 million tonnes of sugar raw value with a probable regional split of 12.1 million tonnes from the centre-south and 3.4 million from the north north-east.
As more of Brazil's cane sector was deregulated the influence of quotas and crop plans was likely to diminish even further, Czarnikow said.
In its first estimate of supply and demand for world sugar in 1997/98, Czarnikow pegged Brazilian sugar production at 15.50 million tonnes raw value after 14.78 million tonnes in 1996/97.
